title: India Tried to Cancel 'India's Got Latent'. It Came Back on Netflix AND YouTube at Once — and Pulled 15 Million in an Afternoon.
excerpt: Samay Raina's roast show was buried by a national controversy in 2025. Season 2's simulcast comeback — with Alia Bhatt and Sharvari judging — is the most-watched second act on the desi internet. The only question left: did the teeth survive the legal battle?
body:
At 7 PM IST on June 20, two things happened at once that have basically never happened before in Indian entertainment. **India's Got Latent**, the show that got buried alive by a national controversy in 2025, walked back onto the internet — and it did it on **YouTube** and **Netflix** at the exact same minute, same length, same chaos, no edits. Fifteen million people showed up within hours. The show that India tried to cancel didn't just survive. It came back bigger, and it brought a streaming giant with it.

If you weren't online for the 2025 implosion, here's the short version. **Samay Raina** built *India's Got Latent* into a phenomenon — a faux-talent show that was really a comedy roast, raw and unfiltered, where contestants performed and a panel of comedians demolished them. It became the most chaotic, most quotable thing on the Indian internet. Then a single comment by podcaster **Ranveer Allahbadia** detonated into FIRs, Supreme Court hearings, and a moral panic that made the show radioactive. Every episode went private on February 12, 2025. For more than a year, it was gone.

> "It was almost uncertain that this show will come back. He has fought countless battles behind the scenes. It was an uphill, almost impossible pipe dream for S2 to even exist." — Ashish Chanchlani, defending the return

The comeback itself is the flex. Raina didn't crawl back quietly — he detonated a record first. His April stand-up special *Still Alive* crossed 53 million views on a single upload, reportedly making it the most-watched full-length stand-up special in the world. Then Netflix India started teasing, posting a cryptic clip of Raina's bodyguard telling fans to spam the comments with lemon and chili emojis. Classic misdirection. By the time the real announcement landed, the internet had already done the marketing for free.

And the format is genuinely a first. *India's Got Latent* Season 2 streams **simultaneously on YouTube and Netflix** — identical runtime, identical content, dropping at the same moment. The only difference? YouTube has ads and a comment section; Netflix is clean and uninterrupted. Raina spelled it out in the announcement video himself, where his friend **Balraj Singh Ghai** accused him of betraying the platform that made him — "certainly not the deed of a true gentleman." It's a clever joke wrapped around a real strategic gamble: keep the free, viral, comment-driven YouTube audience *and* collect the premium Netflix crowd, without forcing anyone to choose.


The premiere guest judges? **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari**, fresh off the *Alpha* trailer becoming India's No. 1 — turning the episode into a promo machine for the first woman-led YRF Spy Universe film. Two of the most-watched women in the country, on the most-watched comeback of the year. That's not a booking, that's a coronation.

Now, the honest part. The discourse since the premiere has been split, and not gently. A loud chunk of the fanbase says S2 feels *filtered* — that the teeth are gone, that the jokes that hit are nowhere near as feral as the ones that got the show cancelled in the first place. Chanchlani fired back on Instagram, reminding everyone that the team "had to fight a year-long legal battle where we promised to stay in line and make sure history doesn't repeat itself." Translation: yes, it's tamer, and that's the price of existing at all. *Kabhi kabhi kuch cheeze karni padti hai.* You take the win.

He's not wrong, but the tension is real, and it's the most interesting thing about this season. The whole appeal of *Latent* was that it felt dangerous, like watching something that wasn't supposed to be allowed. Can a show built on the thrill of crossing the line stay alive once it's promised, in court, never to cross it again? That's the bet Season 2 is making. New episodes drop every two weeks on both platforms.

**For the diaspora, this one's easy.** If you're an NRI in the US, UK, Canada or anywhere with a Netflix subscription, you no longer need a VPN, a sketchy reupload, or a cousin sending you clips on WhatsApp at 3 AM. *India's Got Latent* is now sitting in the same library as your prestige dramas and your true-crime binges — Indian internet comedy, fully legitimized, globally available, no friction. That's a genuinely big deal. The most chaotic show on the desi internet just got a passport.

Whether it's still got its bite is the question. But the fact that it's back at all, on Netflix, pulling fifteen million in an afternoon? Samay Raina already won the round that mattered.
